data treatment

exclusions

##exclude filler, practice, and non-picture trials
exclusions_data <- final_data %>% 
  filter(typeoftrial=="picture" & !(trialcondition %in% c("filler", "practice"))) %>%
  # calculate accuracy
  mutate(accuracy=ifelse(correct=="TRUE",1,0))%>%
  separate(trialcondition, into = c("squashability", "state"))

accuracy analyses

accuracy data

# calculate subject accuracy
subject_accuracy <- exclusions_data %>% group_by(subject) %>% summarise(TaskAccuracy=mean(accuracy))
InaccurateSubjects <- subject_accuracy %>% filter(TaskAccuracy < 0.8)

plot

exclusions_data %>% 
  group_by(squashability, state) %>%
   summarise(ci = list(mean_cl_boot(accuracy) %>% 
                        rename(mean=y, lwr=ymin, upr=ymax))) %>% unnest%>%
  ggplot(aes(x= squashability, y = mean, group = state, fill = state)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.7, color = "gray24")+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lwr, ymax=upr), size = 0.5, width=.15, 
                color = "black", position = position_dodge(0.70))+
  labs(y = "mean accuracy", title = "squashability ratings")+
  theme_clean()+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("darksalmon", "darkslategray4","darkolivegreen4"))+
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(
    color = "white"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(size =rel(2)),
        axis.text = element_text(size =rel(1.5)),
        axis.title = element_text(size =rel(2)),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5, size = rel(1.5)))
## `summarise()` has grouped output by 'squashability'. You can override using the
## `.groups` argument.
## Warning: `cols` is now required when using `unnest()`.
## ℹ Please use `cols = c(ci)`.
## Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
## ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.

main accuracy model

acc_model = glmer(data = exclusions_data, 
                  accuracy ~ squashability + state + (1|subject) + (1|stimulus),
                  family = "binomial")
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
summary(acc_model)
## Generalized linear mixed model fit by maximum likelihood (Laplace
##   Approximation) [glmerMod]
##  Family: binomial  ( logit )
## Formula: accuracy ~ squashability + state + (1 | subject) + (1 | stimulus)
##    Data: exclusions_data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##    700.9    730.1   -345.5    690.9     2515 
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -7.5306  0.0900  0.1289  0.1845  0.9849 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  subject  (Intercept) 1.652    1.285   
##  stimulus (Intercept) 0.000    0.000   
## Number of obs: 2520, groups:  subject, 105; stimulus, 48
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                           Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)                 3.6534     0.2629  13.896  < 2e-16 ***
## squashabilityUnsquashable   0.1825     0.2288   0.798  0.42509    
## stateSmashed                0.7185     0.2383   3.015  0.00257 ** 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) sqshbU
## sqshbltyUns -0.395       
## stateSmashd -0.291  0.005
## optimizer (Nelder_Mead) convergence code: 0 (OK)
## boundary (singular) fit: see help('isSingular')
car::Anova(acc_model)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: accuracy
##                Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)   
## squashability 0.6362  1   0.425092   
## state         9.0891  1   0.002571 **
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

RT analyses

rt data

##exclude incorrect responses
rt_data <- exclusions_data %>% filter(accuracy==1) %>%
  ##exclude subjects with accuracy > 60%
  filter(!subject %in% InaccurateSubjects$subject)

##total participants after exclusion: N = 103 (2 excluded--33%, 58% accuracy)
length(rt_data %>% pull(subject) %>% unique())
## [1] 102

transforming RT

##make rt numeric
rt_data <- rt_data %>% mutate(rt = as.numeric(rt))
## rt histogram ----does NOT look normally distributed (positive skew)
rt_data %>% filter(rt <10000) %>% ggplot(aes(x=rt)) + geom_histogram(binwidth =20, fill="pink" ) + theme_economist() + labs(x="RT (ms)", y="frequency", title= "RT histogram")

##rt log (base 10) transformation
rt_data <- rt_data %>% mutate(log10_rt=log(rt, 10))
##log10(rt) histogram
rt_data %>% ggplot(aes(x=log10_rt)) + geom_histogram(binwidth =0.1, fill="pink" ) + theme_economist() + labs(x="log10(rt)", y="frequency", title= "RT histogram")

##looks fairly normal now

MAD exclusions

mad_data = rt_data %>%
  group_by(squashability, state) %>%
  mutate(MAD=3*mad(log10_rt), med=median(log10_rt),
         L= (med - MAD), U=(med + MAD)) %>%
  filter(log10_rt < U) %>% filter(log10_rt > L)

(nrow(data)-nrow(mad_data))/nrow(data)
## numeric(0)

plot

mad_data %>% 
  group_by(squashability, state) %>%
   summarise(ci = list(mean_cl_boot(rt) %>% 
                        rename(mean=y, lwr=ymin, upr=ymax))) %>% unnest%>%
  ggplot(aes(x= squashability, y = mean, group = state, fill = state)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge", width = 0.7, color = "gray24")+

main RT model

rt_model = lmer(data = mad_data, 
                log10_rt ~ squashability*state + (squashability |subject) + (1|stimulus))
summary(rt_model)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: log10_rt ~ squashability * state + (squashability | subject) +  
##     (1 | stimulus)
##    Data: mad_data
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: -2956.2
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -3.9811 -0.6365 -0.1008  0.5076  5.1763 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name                      Variance  Std.Dev. Corr
##  subject  (Intercept)               0.0138334 0.11762      
##           squashabilityUnsquashable 0.0002398 0.01549  0.37
##  stimulus (Intercept)               0.0011563 0.03400      
##  Residual                           0.0138541 0.11770      
## Number of obs: 2353, groups:  subject, 102; stimulus, 48
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                                          Estimate Std. Error         df t value
## (Intercept)                             2.879e+00  1.599e-02  1.185e+02 180.078
## squashabilityUnsquashable              -2.474e-02  1.557e-02  4.334e+01  -1.589
## stateSmashed                           -9.381e-04  1.549e-02  4.271e+01  -0.061
## squashabilityUnsquashable:stateSmashed  4.386e-02  2.191e-02  4.268e+01   2.002
##                                        Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)                              <2e-16 ***
## squashabilityUnsquashable                0.1194    
## stateSmashed                             0.9520    
## squashabilityUnsquashable:stateSmashed   0.0516 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) sqshbU sttSms
## sqshbltyUns -0.455              
## stateSmashd -0.484  0.497       
## sqshbltyU:S  0.342 -0.704 -0.707
car::Anova(rt_model)
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)

posthoc models

# split into picture type (state)
intact_data = mad_data %>% filter(state == "Normal")
squashed_data = mad_data %>% filter(state == "Smashed")

# run separate models on these data

intact_model = lmer(data = intact_data, log10_rt ~ squashability + (squashability | subject) + 
                      (1 | stimulus))
summary(intact_model)

Demographic Info

demo = final_data %>% filter(typeoftrial %in% c("demo", "english") & response != "0") %>%
  separate(response, into = c("demo1", "demo2", "demo3", "demo4"), sep = ":")
## Warning: Expected 4 pieces. Missing pieces filled with `NA` in 361 rows [2, 4, 5, 7, 9,
## 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 29, 30, 32, 34, ...].
age = demo %>% filter(demo1 == "{\"Age\"") %>% select(demo2) %>%
  mutate(age = as.numeric(gsub("[^[:digit:] ]", "", demo2)))
age %>% summarise(mean_age = mean(age))
